ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, O is on the left side, OM is a horizontal dashed line to the right, and ON is a dashed line inclined from O toward the upper right; the angle between the two lines is marked as 30°. The area above OM is filled with dot symbols and labeled B, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. Near a certain point on OM, the particle enters the magnetic field obliquely toward the upper left with velocity v, and the angle between the velocity direction and OM is marked as 30°. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the problem statement and the figure, take O as the origin and OM as the positive direction of the x-axis, then the equation of ON is y=x/√3. Suppose the particle enters from A=(a,0), and the trajectory radius is r=mv/(qB). The particle is positively charged, the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward, and the velocity is obliquely toward the upper left, so the Lorentz force points toward the upper right; the center of the circle is therefore to the upper right of A and perpendicular to the velocity, so the center C=(a+r/2, √3r/2). The trajectory circle equation is (x-a-r/2)^2+(y-√3r/2)^2=r^2. It is known that the trajectory has only one intersection point with ON, that is, the line y=x/√3 is tangent to the circle. Write the line as x-√3y=0, and the distance from the center C to this line is |(a+r/2)-√3(√3r/2)|/2=|a-r|/2. Tangency requires |a-r|/2=r, so a=3r or a=-r. The incident point is on the right side of O, take a=3r. The exit point is the other intersection point of this circle with OM, namely y=0. Let y=0, obtaining (x-a-r/2)^2+3r^2/4=r^2, so x=a or x=a+r. The other intersection point is x=a+r=4r. Therefore the distance from the exit point to O is 4r=4mv/(qB).
